section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Henselianity and the strength of the isogeny conclusion
body: “Pourquoi S hensélien ?” has a doubtful adjective, while “pourquoi seulement à isogénie près ?” explicitly distinguishes the case $\ell\ne p$. These are requests to separate the hypotheses needed to construct the objects from the hypotheses needed for an integral, rather than rational, comparison; the isolated remark does not establish a stronger theorem.
context: Adds an earlier hypothesis audit to CT N38–N43 (36/073–077), and bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N97; the later adic-base argument is a comparison lead, not an answer to every introductory objection.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: An unsupported cohomological remark is challenged
body: The assessments “il semble clair … est un peu optimiste” and “ni fondé sur des théorèmes” explicitly deny that the cited draft passages have an adequate justification. Since the $H^i$ remark being criticized is not supplied here, its content and truth value cannot be reconstructed from the objection alone.
context: Adds a direct authorial warning to the S19 comparison requested in README and RS MPL_33_002-049 §2; no matching statement of the criticized remark occurs in CT.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Semistable and stable reduction need distinct references
body: The request “une référence ou définition pour réduction semi-stable d’une courbe” says that reference [3] uses only stable reduction terminology. A print comparison must identify both the cited definition and the operation by which one passes between the two kinds of model, without treating this editorial question as a denial of the reduction theorem.
context: Adds a terminology question to README S19 and differs from CT N97 (36/073–079), which concerns an orthogonality argument, not the definition of a semistable curve.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Epimorphism is not the definition being requested
body: “épimorphisme n’est pas la définition d’isogénie” flags an omitted finiteness condition or an unstated categorical convention, and the same block proposes “quasi projectif” in place of “séparé type fini”. The underlying draft proposition is absent, so these are two local corrections to check against its exact group-scheme category, not a license to replace all finite-type hypotheses by quasi-projectivity.
context: Adds source-specific comparison tasks to README S19; CT N39 (36/074) also makes finite-type and étaleness hypotheses consequential, but does not settle these corrections.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Comparison with the Artin–Mazur pairing is expressly unverified
body: “As tu vérifié si l’accouplement d’A. M. coïncide avec le tien ?” asks for equality of constructions, not merely agreement of their ranks or perfectness. The initials remain doubtful in the transcription, but the context’s explicit Artin–Mazur title makes that expansion a strong research lead, with normalization and signs still to compare.
context: Adds an earlier explicit comparison request to CT N57–N59 and its title inventory (36/082–084); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N57 and N59 without certifying their geometric identification.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Formal unramifiedness and separable closure are questioned
body: The isolated questions “formellement non ramifié ?” and “séparablement clos ?” ask which precise hypotheses or notions are intended. The following complaint about the absence of a reference makes it especially unsafe to supply a stronger smoothness, étaleness, or algebraic-closure assumption from later theory.
context: Adds an unresolved definition-and-hypothesis audit to README S19; CT N38–N42 (36/073–077) concern a different lifting argument and cannot retrospectively fix these words.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Strictness of the weight filtration and detection of isogenies
body: For torus-by-abelian extensions, the note asserts that a morphism is “strictement compatible à la filtration par … poids” and is an isogeny exactly when its $T_\ell$ map is one. A proof must specify the base field, the meaning of an isogeny of Tate modules, and why a statement on the toric and abelian graded pieces controls both kernel and cokernel.
context: Adds a proposed replacement argument to CT N40–N41 and N49 (36/075–079); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N97, while differing from a claim that bilinear vanishing alone gives an orthogonal complement.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: The exact remark 2.6(a) is already under scrutiny
body: “S est-il un trait dans cette remarque ; sait-on assez sur le passage à la limite et Néron ?” attaches two proof obligations to Remark 2.6(a). The question is valuable because it identifies a precise draft locator at which one must check the trait reduction and compatibility of the Néron construction with the limit, rather than invoke the weight argument abstractly.
context: Adds an explicit earlier criticism of the same numbered comparison cited by CT N97 (36/073–079); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N97, whose reported print check remains an earlier run’s claim here.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Torsion kernels, specialization and a doubtful generic subscript
body: The proposed simplification ${}_nK=\ker({}_nG\to{}_nH)$ is followed by a proposed subgroup relation between specialized fibres and the question “dim Ker($u_\eta$)=0 ?”, with $s$ an alternative to $\eta$. These require the actual torsion-sheaf topology and specialization maps; the preferred generic subscript must not be changed to the special fibre because that would make a familiar argument.
context: Adds a kernel-level precursor to CT N39 (36/074), which reports finite étale lifting of torsion; neither its different setup nor RS MPL_91_099-143 §68 supplies the missing specialization hypotheses.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Inertia outside the henselian setting
body: “Les notions … ont elles été définies pour S non hensélien ?” is followed by the concrete requirement “choisir un groupe d’inertie”. A reconstruction should distinguish an object defined after a choice of geometric point or valuation from a choice-independent object descended to the original base.
context: Adds a definitional issue to CT N38 and N45 (36/073–077, 081), where adic and strictly henselian versions differ; bears on README S19, not on a new solution of an arithmetic section problem.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: A tubular-neighbourhood statement is proposed in a ringed topos
body: After asking for an “énoncé style ‘voisinage tubulaire’ compréhensible”, the note describes a morphism of étale topoi and a relative scheme with a pulled-back structure sheaf. The base letter in the relative topos and the small adjoining annotation are doubtful, so establishing the direction of inverse and direct image and the relevant ring object is prior to any geometric interpretation.
context: Adds an explicit topos-level formulation to README S19 and differs from CT N62–N79 (39/004, 010–015), which concern formal inverse-function axioms rather than this Néron neighbourhood.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: The trace/contragredient correction is contested
location: draft p 36, line −6 and pencil mark
body: The live sentence says that the trace is not what is contragredient and that “l’énoncé primitif était correct”, beside a doubtful “si ?”. This records a local dispute about the direction of duality; neither the original statement nor an unambiguous resolution of the pencil response is supplied.
context: Adds a source-level comparison issue to CT N53 and N57 (36/084), where transpose and geometric duality are distinguished; bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N57 only as a normalization lead.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Killed by ell versus ell-primary torsion
body: “$\ell$-groupe signifie-t-il tué par $\ell$, ou par un $\ell^n$ ?” exposes a distinction that changes the range of every finite-level statement in that paragraph. The same block asks whether the trait is strictly local and requests an identifiable “loc cit.”; none of those conventions is established by the excerpt.
context: Adds an explicit terminology warning to CT N21–N26 (36/061–063, 071), whose finite exponent and inverse-limit distinctions are closely related; the later notes do not answer the missing reference.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Dirac normalization can be checked independently
body: The two displayed alternatives are $f(e)=1$ and $f(e)=\#G$, both zero elsewhere. For normalized counting measure $|G|^{-1}\sum_g$, their integrals are respectively $|G|^{-1}$ and $1$, whereas ordinary counting measure reverses which is the unit-mass convention. This elementary calculation explains why a definition of the measure, rather than quotation marks alone, is needed.
context: Adds a concrete normalization test to CT N14–N16 (36/066–072), which describe reused Haar-measure material; it does not identify that source with the draft criticized here.
reason: direct evaluation of the two finite sums; no geometric hypothesis is used

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: The n=2 and non-strictly-local proof is distrusted
body: “je n’ai pas confiance en dehors du cas strictement local” explicitly limits confidence in the proof, and the preceding words single out $n=2$. Because the criticized proof is absent, the next task is to identify its descent step and its use of a chosen splitting, rather than manufacture a counterexample from the numeral 2.
context: Adds an explicit proof warning to README S19; CT N30 (36/067) also isolates a local lifting argument, but concerns roots of line bundles and is not a resolution of 4.7.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Pro-objects or schemes is an actual categorical question
body: “S’agit-il de pro-objets, ou de schémas” questions both a formula and the phrase “par définition”, while the margin replies “je le dis !”. The response shows disagreement about exposition, but does not determine the intended category in this excerpt.
context: Adds an earlier categorical warning to CT N25 and N47 (36/063, 079–080), and to the projective-system distinction on current scans 032 and 050; it does not collapse those three uses of limits into one theorem.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: The criticism of 5.7 is withdrawn locally
body: The judgment that 5.7 is a repetition for $\ell\ne p$ and “un peu idiot” for $\ell=p$ is crossed out, while “utilisé en 5.15” remains. Both the criticism and its withdrawal occur on scan 006, so the surviving annotation is evidence of a dependency, not a live rejection of the result.
context: Adds a documented withdrawal to README S19; differs from CT N26 (36/062–063), where a restriction is removed through a new obstruction argument, not through this dependency note.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Characteristic hypotheses must be traced through the dependency
body: The note says that $\operatorname{car}(k)\ne\ell$ is no longer needed in 5.15, but insists that 6.6 uses $\operatorname{car}(K)=0$ “via Tate”; the margin answers that this is stated in the hypotheses of 5.15. This distinguishes residue characteristic from fraction-field characteristic and asks whether a proof dependency transports the correct assumption.
context: Adds an explicit dependency audit to CT N26 (36/062–063) and RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N97; the later enlargement of a coefficient range does not remove the cited Tate hypothesis.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Divisibility and the discrete part cannot be alternated silently
body: “tu supposes tantôt $A^0$ $\ell$-divisible … tantôt non” and “Que fais-tu de la partie discrète ?” flag two omitted structural distinctions. They must be tested before identifying a connected $p$-divisible part with a complete torsion object or applying a limit argument to it.
context: Adds direct warnings to CT N39 and N47 (36/074, 079–080), where finite torsion lifts and compatible towers are separate; also bears on the present divisibility qualifications on 050.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: The manuscript calls 6.3 false and gives a deformation strategy
body: “6.3 est faux” is followed by the proposal to deform $E\times F$, with $E$ ordinary and $F$ nonordinary elliptic, to a generically simple abelian variety. The disputed assertion is the lifting of the largest ordinary abelian subvariety, and the page sketches rather than proves the required deformation and generic simplicity.
context: Adds a specific claimed counterexample absent from CT; CT N39–N49 (36/074–080) concern torsion/orthogonality and do not certify or refute this algebraic lifting claim, so README S19 remains the relevant register task.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: What would complete the proposed deformation counterexample
body: A rigorous version of “générique simple” would choose a family specializing to $E\times F$ whose geometric generic fibre has no positive-dimensional proper abelian subvariety, then show that a lift of the ordinary elliptic factor would supply precisely such a subvariety. The distinction between an algebraic abelian subvariety and a formal or $p$-divisible subgroup is essential, since the latter need not contradict generic simplicity. This supplies a proof plan conditional on the existence and specialization properties of the chosen family, not a completed counterexample.
context: Adds a narrowly defined test beyond CT N39–N49 (36/074–080); no context claim settles this deformation problem, and no status change in RS is proposed.
reason: the contradiction from an algebraic lifted factor is clear, but the required family and extension argument have not been constructed here

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Finite and toric parts up to isogeny are an expectation
body: “Il me semble qu’il doit être possible de définir, à isogénie près” introduces finite and toric parts “ayant le bon rang”. The nearby “non, mon argument marche” records a reply, but its attachment does not make a proof of that proposed construction visible here.
context: Adds an explicit expectation to CT N40–N49 (36/075–080); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N97, while the rank/saturation distinction in CT N49 prevents mistaking the later vanishing argument for this construction.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: The limits of the editorial reading are themselves recorded
body: “Je n’ai ps confiance en ‘il est immédiat’ de 6.4” is answered “c’est pourtant trivial”, and the next entry explicitly says “Je n’ai pas lu”. These marks document an unresolved proof dispute and a stated reading boundary; the latter is not an omitted page of the present transcription.
context: Adds an evidential limitation to README S19 and differs from CT N45 (36/081), whose entire cancelled draft is visible in the earlier package; neither note licenses filling an unseen argument.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: The Serre reference concerns an uncertain abbreviation
body: The primary reading is “l’indép. de $\ell$”, with “l’insép.” retained as an alternative, followed by a complaint that 6.6 is used in 5.13. A bibliography search should therefore start with independence of $\ell$ while preserving the palaeographic alternative and the unresolved draft-page number.
context: Adds a precise reading constraint to CT N97 (36/073–079) and README S19; no Serre citation in the supplied context resolves the abbreviation.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Strict henselianity and excellence are explicit open hypotheses
body: “S strictement hensélien ?” is justified by a later use in the draft, and “pas d’hyp. d’excellence ?” asks about a separate base condition. These should be audited independently: a reference to strict locality does not supply excellence, and neither question asserts that both hypotheses are necessary.
context: Adds exact local hypothesis questions to CT N38, N42, N45 (36/073–077, 081) and RS MPL_91_099-143 §68; the Greenberg/Néron excerpt does not specify an answer.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Compatibility with R and a possible sign remain unchecked
body: “compatibilité avec R ?” and the requested qualification “au signe près” leave functoriality and normalization as separate verification tasks. A comparison of perfect pairings alone cannot decide either, because an overall sign preserves perfectness.
context: Adds an earlier sign warning to CT N53–N57 (36/083–084); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N57 and N59, with CT N55 offering only a later proposed sign test.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: A field enlargement and promised verifications need justification
body: “Une extension de K (qui ici est infini) est-elle requise ??” questions the construction’s field enlargement, and “Dire où on fera ces vérifications” asks for a located proof. The infinity of the field is a proposed simplification, not a demonstrated replacement for every extension used by the unseen construction.
context: Adds an explicit extension-and-proof-location question to CT N48 (36/080), where K is enlarged but not renamed in a formula; the two issues are comparable but not identical.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Commutation of the Néron model with completion needs a source
body: “Dire où on trouve que Néron commute à $S\mapsto\widehat S$” requests a specific base-change theorem. Its useful reconstruction must state the trait, residue-field, and finiteness assumptions and identify the comparison morphism, rather than treating completion as an automatic operation on all smooth models.
context: Adds a concrete reference request to CT N30, N42, N52 (36/067, 074–075, 083); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N52 and MPL_91_099-143 §68, whose excerpts do not furnish the theorem.

section: I. Editorial remarks on SGA 7 IX (003–008)
title: Extension from ell-primary torsion is stated as a question to the draft
body: After objecting to a proof left to the reader, the note paraphrases the claim that extending a biextension to $A\times A'$ is “la $\hat m$ chose” as extending it to the $\ell$-primary torsion subgroups. The assertion needs an equivalence of extension data, with its torsion and component-group hypotheses, rather than merely agreement of pairings on a Tate module.
context: Adds the earlier explicit question behind CT N57 and N97 (36/084 and 073–079); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N57, N97, but their reported extension obstruction is not independently established by this question.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The lattice–torus diagram suggests dual two-term objects
body: The labels $T=D(M')$, $T'=D(M)$ and the later complexes $[M\to G]$ organize the sheets around lattice and semiabelian data. This is a useful route to comparing dual 1-motives, but the headless strokes and the left-pointing terminal arrow on 028 must not be promoted into an exact-sequence assertion that the ink does not make.
context: Adds a lattice–torus precursor to CT N06–N12 (36/054–058); the closest supplied RS entry, MPL_36_053-085+39 §113, is a comparison inventory rather than a theorem about 1-motives.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The extension construction uses two different internal vanishings
body: The sheet passes from maps into internal Ext to extensions by $D(M)$ and $D(M')$, and annotates the example with both a Hom-vanishing and an internal Ext-vanishing. A proof must keep these two roles separate and verify them after base change; the annotations do not justify replacing an internal sheaf by its global sections.
context: Adds the construction preceding CT N06–N07 (36/054), which likewise distinguish sheaf-Hom rigidity from global classification; bears on README S19, with no supplied reviewed result closing this step.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: Compatibility of the two splittings is the surviving criterion
body: The live criterion says that two lifts correspond exactly when the two induced splittings “coïncident” on $\mathcal E_{M,M'}$. The longer crossed formulation should be read as a discarded presentation, while the surviving compatibility is the datum a descent construction must use.
context: Adds an explicit double-rigidification compatibility to CT N07–N08 (36/054–056); the later additivity claim is related but does not replace the equality of splittings required here.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The derived biextension class is proposed beside pourquoi
location: complexes, canonical class and aborted proof
body: The passage replaces an ordinary quotient by complexes in degrees −1, 0 and proposes a “classe canonique” in $\operatorname{Ext}^1(A\otimes^L A',G_m)$. The aborted “Soit en effet” and marginal doubtful “pourquoi ?” leave the construction or its justification visibly unfinished; one should not read the surrounding notation as a completed proof.
context: Adds a direct homological construction problem to CT N06–N08 (36/054–056); no earlier context result proves this class exists with the stated rigidifications.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: A precise published comparison for the two-term construction
body: Deligne (1974, §10.2.1, p. 60) defines biextensions of two-term complexes using two compatible trivializations and identifies their degree 0 and 1 groups with derived-tensor Ext. This is a precise comparator for “coïncident” on 029 and “jouant le rôle d’une biextension” on 031; it does not date these sheets or show that their incomplete argument was already complete.
context: Adds an independently checked primary comparison to README S19 and differs from CT N06–N08 (36/054–056), whose subject is rigidity of torsor descriptions; bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 §115 as additional bibliography.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: An explicit model tests the torsion exact sequence
location: definition of the n-torsion object and first exact sequence
body: For $A=[M\xrightarrow{u}G]$, define $V_n=\{(m,g):u(m)=ng\}/\{(nm',u(m'))\}$ in the chosen sheaf category. If ${}_nM=0$ and multiplication by $n$ on $G$ is an epimorphism, projection to $m\bmod n$ gives $0\to{}_nG\to V_n\to M/nM\to0$, directly checking the two hypotheses written on 031. Comparing $V_n$ with the manuscript’s internal $\operatorname{Ext}^0(\mathbb Z/n,A)$ still requires the same derived-degree convention, rather than a silent definition change.
context: Adds a concrete verification method to CT N06–N08 (36/054–056); no context note supplies this torsion model, and README S19 is the relevant plan entry.
reason: kernel and local surjectivity follow directly from the displayed presentation under the two stated assumptions

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The limit sequence needs its own exactness check
body: “passant à la limite sur $n=\ell^\nu$” turns the finite sequences into Tate sequences without a separate limit argument. One must state whether this is an exact sequence of systems, sheaves, or inverse limits of sections and check the corresponding lifting condition; the first term in the second row is frozen as $T_\ell(A'|G')$, so its expected $G'$ is only a reading alternative.
context: Adds a further instance to CT N25 and N43 (36/063, 076–077), which already flag transition maps and uniformity; it restates the need for such control without transferring their geometric hypotheses.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The local maps in the pairing construction must glue
body: The local maps from the torsion objects into the complexes are followed by the doubtful words “qui se recollent” and a claimed global homomorphism. The proof obligation is independence of the local lifts, compatibility on overlaps, and the precise passage from an Ext class to the displayed Hom group, not merely the existence of local representatives.
context: Adds a descent problem to CT N06–N08 (36/054–056), where rigidity could control uniqueness; it does not establish the needed vanishing solely from the later wording “est discrète”.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The induced graded pairings are asserted without calculation
body: The orthogonality statements are followed by “sont ceux qu’on devine” for the induced lattice–torus and abelian pairings, then a perfectness corollary with explicit torsion and divisibility assumptions. The small parenthetical torsion indices are doubtful, so the task is to verify each graded pairing and exact sequence before invoking the corollary, not to repair its hypotheses by expectation.
context: Adds a filtered-duality calculation to CT N49 (36/073–079), which distinguishes vanishing from equality; bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N97, but the present perfectness claim has different data.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: A filtered proof would isolate what perfectness still needs
body: If the two torsion objects have finite filtrations with the stated opposite orthogonality and perfect pairings on matching graded pieces, exactness of the appropriate duality functor gives perfectness of the total pairing by induction on the filtration. This reduces the corollary to the explicit graded identifications and exactness hypotheses, which remain to be checked in the source’s sheaf category. It does not derive equality of orthogonal complements from vanishing alone.
context: Adds a proof organization to CT N49 and differs from the component-lattice construction of CT N54 (36/084); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N97 only through the common orthogonality issue.
reason: the filtered isomorphism argument is formal once exact duality and the graded isomorphisms are assumed

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The typed pairing text has its own reading order
body: The title “Accouplements définis par une biextension” on 034 begins the typed sequence, continued on 032 and then 030. The archive scan order is preserved in the transcription, but a mathematical comparison must follow 034→032→030 and acknowledge that 030 stops at “Or cette compatibilité résulte de”.
context: Adds an internal order distinct from CT’s reused-type pagination inventory (36/053, 055, 057, 059, 066–072); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 §111 and §113 without inferring a composition chronology.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: The asymmetric compatibility is stronger than the doubled one
body: The live text explicitly removes a restriction on $Q$ for the asymmetric identity $\phi^n(mx,y)=\phi^{n'}(x,y)$, and uses it to recover the doubly multiplied formula. The displayed membership $y\in{}_{n'}P(S)$ on 032 and the mismatched indices on 030 are retained literally; proving the compatibility requires independently matching each domain and the Tor boundary maps.
context: Adds the finite-level mechanism needed beside CT N47 (36/079–080), which records nonvanishing before taking limits; the context does not repair the printed P/Q or n/n′ discrepancies.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: A proof formerly left to the reader is promised explicitly
body: On 034 “qu’on laisse au lecteur le soin d’établir” is deleted and replaced by “cf. 2.3 ci-dessous pour une démonstration”. Scans 032 and 030 provide the stronger compatibility and a Tor-based proof route, although the retained endpoint is incomplete. This is a withdrawal of a proof deferral across 034→032→030, not a retraction of the compatibility statement.
context: Adds a documented editorial repair to CT N31 (36/067, 069), where proof routes also change; bears on README S19 and differs from simply counting every cancelled proof as a withdrawn theorem.

section: II. Complexes, biextensions and torsion pairings (028–034)
title: Tate notation expressly denotes a projective system here
body: Scan 032 defines $T_\ell(M)=({}_{\ell^\nu}M)_\nu$ as a “système projectif”, and 050 insists on retaining finite-level pairings when stronger divisibility is unavailable. This distinction connects the construction of the pairing to the later warnings about what can disappear after passing to a limit, without identifying a strict diagram of groups, an object in a pro-category, and its inverse-limit group.
context: Adds explicit categorical language to CT N25 and N47 (36/063, 079–080); bears on README S19 and qualifies any use of CT’s “projective-limit pairing” as complete finite-level data.

section: III. Picard duality, adjunction and characteristic-p comparisons (035–046)
title: The cohomology table does not state its hypotheses
body: The table invokes “l’autodualité de P” and “la dualité de Kummer-Serre”, but this sheet supplies no condition on $X$, its dimension, its base field, or the topology. Its Jacobian wording strongly suggests a curve calculation; that inference is a research interpretation, and cannot turn the three-row table into a theorem for every proper scheme.
context: Adds a cohomological precursor to CT N57–N59 and its Artin–Mazur cover (36/082–084); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N59, with the curve hypotheses of that comparison still distinct.

section: III. Picard duality, adjunction and characteristic-p comparisons (035–046)
title: Three characteristic-p coefficient objects must stay separate
location: p row and bottom Frobenius row
body: The frozen coefficient forms are $\zeta_p$, $\mathbb Z/p$, and a dotted $i_p$ with $\alpha_p$ as an alternative, and the left middle cell literally repeats $H^2(X,\mathbb Z/p)$. A useful comparison tests the Kummer, Artin–Schreier, and Frobenius-kernel sequences separately, retaining the distinction between flat and étale cohomology (The Stacks Project, 2026a, tag 0A3J; The Stacks Project, 2026e, tag 03PK). This can constrain a mathematical interpretation but cannot identify the uncertain glyph or correct the repeated formula after the freeze.
context: Adds a coefficient-and-topology warning to CT N24–N26 (36/063), whose p-primary Brauer correction also depends on the chosen sequence; no CT reading settles the three glyphs.

section: III. Picard duality, adjunction and characteristic-p comparisons (035–046)
title: The local-to-global sketch uses an exclamation mark
location: top Ext diagram and programme list
body: The upper diagram writes $f_!$, while the programme below includes “Dualité de Cartier” and a highly uncertain final question ending “??”. A modern adjunction might suggest $Rf_*$ in one interpretation, but the visible exclamation mark and the separate star notation on 043 remain frozen; the correct functors and ambient categories are research questions.
context: Adds a functor-level ambiguity to CT N06–N08 (36/054–056); bears on README S19 and differs from simply substituting the modern adjoint expected from the formula.

section: III. Picard duality, adjunction and characteristic-p comparisons (035–046)
title: The assertion that H¹ with abelian coefficients is torsion comes first
location: opening line after X and A
body: For “X propre et simple”, the page begins with $H^1(X,A)=\varinjlim_n{}_nH^1(X,A)$. section: IV. Reconstruction from torsion and rigidity of torsors (047–052)
title: A bounded factor can erase a nonzero pairing at the limit

With a generator of $Q[\ell^r]$ represented by $1/\ell^r$, the bilinear maps $\phi_r(x,y/\ell^r)=xy/\ell\bmod\mathbb Z$ are nonzero and satisfy the simultaneous multiplication compatibility, yet induce zero on inverse limits. This supplies an explicit algebraic model for the lost finite-level data; identifying these classes with biextensions uses the derived-tensor comparison, and does not establish the full manuscript equivalence.

section: IV. Reconstruction from torsion and rigidity of torsors (047–052)
title: Rigidity can force coherence of a primitive torsor law
location: essential-image criterion using pi-star and projections
body: Under universal vanishing of pointed maps $A\to G$, the same vanishing holds for $A^r$ by subtracting the value at zero in one coordinate at a time. For a rigidified torsor with an isomorphism $\pi^*L\simeq\operatorname{pr}_1^*L\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*L$, normalize that isomorphism at the origin; its two associativity composites and its transpose then differ by pointed maps from $A^3$ or $A^2$ to $G$, so are equal. This gives a route from the primitive class condition to a unique commutative extension law, provided the vanishing is genuinely internal and base-change stable.

title: The Artin–Mazur and sign questions suggest a small comparison experiment
body: Fix a single convention for the Poincaré biextension and compute the induced torsion pairing on an elliptic curve, then compare it with the cup-product convention used for the Artin–Mazur construction. Such a calculation could detect a sign or Tate-twist normalization invisible to perfectness alone and supply a preliminary check before the component-group comparison. It would not by itself prove the general compatibility or identify the weighted discriminant form.
context: Adds a concrete test prompted by “coïncide” and “au signe près” to CT N55, N57–N59 (36/083–084); bears on RS MPL_36_053-085+39 N57, N59, while leaving their geometric bridge open.
reason: a small example can distinguish normalizations, but a universal comparison needs naturality and degeneration arguments

section: VI. Cross-package comparisons and limits of the supplied plan
title: The supplied subject placement is confirmed but is incomplete
location: title and cover sheets; rigidity heading
body: “Remarques. SGA 7 IX”, “Picard et dualité”, and “biextensions de faisceaux de groupes” confirm the README’s SGA-draft placement. The retained sheets also contain two-term complexes, a tentative higher-Picard duality programme, and unrelated reused Lie/Čech texts, so a monodromy-only description misses substantial content.
context: Adds an observed scope correction to README S19 and RS MPL_33_002-049 §2; complements CT’s covers at 36/060, 073, 082 recorded in RS MPL_36_053-085+39 §111.

section: VI. Cross-package comparisons and limits of the supplied plan
title: Shared obstruction language does not settle the arithmetic register
location: derived class, higher-Picard sketch, rigidity sequence
body: The present Ext, torsion and obstruction constructions are structurally suggestive but do not give the image or fibres of the marked depth-two arithmetic section maps. Likewise, none of these sheets states the residue complex or convergence criterion of the class-two germ return, so no proof transfer follows merely from the common word “obstruction”.
context: Differs from RS LM7 E.23 [Open, return’s claim], LM7_PUSH C.6 [Proved, return’s claim] and INTAKE LM7_CONTINUED §? [intake, not referee verdict]; adds no change of status or re-derivation of those entries.
